forms: which group does this go in
MATH.G1.NUMBER.PRE_NUMBER_ACTIVITIES.SOR.mastery: The child sorts a mixed collection into groups by one attribute (colour, size, shape, use or texture), says the rule used, and finds the object that does not belong in a group.
MATH.G1.NUMBER.PRE_NUMBER_ACTIVITIES.SOR.hands_on: Collecting and sorting real objects is done in class.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.PRE_NUMBER_ACTIVITIES.MAT.mastery: The child pairs objects that share an attribute (a shoe with a shoe, a big stone with a big stone, things used together such as a cup and a saucer), and says why they match.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.PRE_NUMBER_ACTIVITIES.ORD.mastery: The child arranges three to five objects from smallest to biggest (or shortest to longest, lightest to heaviest) and the reverse, and names the first and last.

forms: what is missing in the pattern
MATH.G1.NUMBER.PRE_NUMBER_ACTIVITIES.OBJ.mastery: The child copies, continues and makes a repeating pattern with real objects (bottle tops, leaves, beads) by colour, size or shape, and says what comes next.
MATH.G1.NUMBER.PRE_NUMBER_ACTIVITIES.OBJ.hands_on: Making patterns with real objects is done in class.

forms: missing number in a forward count
MATH.G1.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.COUNT_FORWA.mastery: Starting from any number, the child counts on in ones to 50 (and in twos to 20), saying each number once, crossing each ten correctly (19, 20, 21), and says the number after any number.

forms: missing number in a backward count
MATH.G1.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.COUNT_BACK_.mastery: The child counts back in ones from 30 or from any number up to 30, crossing each ten correctly (21, 20, 19), and says the number before.

forms: match the group to the number
show the number with bottle tops
MATH.G1.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.REPRESENT_3.mastery: The child counts out a given number of objects up to 30, touching each once, and matches a group of objects to its number, keeping track by moving each object as it is counted.
MATH.G1.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.REPRESENT_3.hands_on: Counting real objects is done in class.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.READ_WRITE_.mastery: The child reads any number up to 50 and writes numbers to 50 in symbols with digits facing the right way and in the right order (14, not 41).

forms: match the word to the number
MATH.G1.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.WORDS_10.mastery: The child reads and writes the number words one to ten with correct spelling and matches each word to its numeral and to a group of objects.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.NUMBER_PATT.mastery: The child finds the missing number in a counting pattern going up or down in ones or twos up to 20 (2, 4, __, 8), and says the jump. Counting in fives and tens is met in the older practice families.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.ADDITION.MODEL_ADDITION.mastery: The child puts two groups of objects together and counts all of them to find how many there are now, and tells a 'had some, got some more' story for it (3 birds and 2 more birds is 5 birds).

forms: match the picture to the sentence
MATH.G1.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_SIGNS.mastery: The child writes an addition statement for a picture or story with + and = in the right places (3 + 2 = 5) and reads it as 'three add two equals five'.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_TWO_SINGLE.mastery: The child adds two single-digit numbers (7 + 5 = 12) by counting on from the larger, using fingers, objects or a number line, in stories and number sentences. Games with dice and devices are played in class.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_THREE_SINGLE.mastery: The child adds three single-digit numbers (4 + 3 + 5 = 12) by adding two first and then the third, or by finding a pair that makes ten.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_2D_1D_50.mastery: The child adds a 1-digit number to a 2-digit number when the ones do not make ten (23 + 4 = 27), across or in a column, using an abacus or number cards, with the sum up to 50.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_MISSING_50.mastery: The child finds the missing number in an adding pattern (5, 7, 9, __) or in an addition (6 + __ = 10, how many more are needed) by counting up from the number known.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.MODEL_SUBTRAC.mastery: The child takes some objects away from a group and counts what is left (8 sweets, 3 given away, 5 left), and tells a 'had some, gave some away' story for it.

forms: match the picture to the sentence
MATH.G1.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_SIGNS.mastery: The child writes a subtraction sentence for a picture or story with - and = in the right places, with the starting number first (8 - 3 = 5), and reads it.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_SINGLE.mastery: The child takes a single-digit number from a number up to 18 (13 - 5 = 8) by counting back, using objects or a number line, or from a known addition fact (5 + 8 = 13). Games are played in class.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_2D_1D_NO_.mastery: The child takes a 1-digit number from a 2-digit number when the ones digit is big enough (37 - 4 = 33), across or in a column, with number cards or a chart.

MATH.G1.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_MISSING_5.mastery: The child continues or fills in a pattern that goes down by the same number (20, 18, 16, __) and finds a missing number in a subtraction (some were eaten, 5 are left from 12: how many were eaten?).

MATH.G1.MEASUR.LENGTH.COMPARE_LENGTH.mastery: The child collects objects of different lengths, lines up one end of two objects, and says which is longer than, shorter than or the same as the other; finds the longest and shortest of three.
MATH.G1.MEASUR.LENGTH.COMPARE_LENGTH.hands_on: Collecting objects from the environment is done in class.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_ARBITRARY_.mastery: The child measures a length with hand spans, steps, sticks or pencils laid end to end without gaps, counts the units, and says why two children's hand-span counts for the same desk can differ.
MATH.G1.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_ARBITRARY_.hands_on: Measuring with hand spans and steps is done in class.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.MASS.COMPARE_MASS.mastery: The child holds two objects and says which is heavier, lighter or about the same, and puts three objects in order from two comparisons (if the cow is heavier than the goat and the goat heavier than the hen, the cow is heaviest).
MATH.G1.MEASUR.MASS.COMPARE_MASS.hands_on: Collecting and holding objects is done in class.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_ARBITRARY_MA.mastery: The child measures how many cups or tins of beans or maize balance an object, or how many tins of a known mass make a bag, and counts the units.
MATH.G1.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_ARBITRARY_MA.hands_on: Measuring with containers of beans or maize is done in class.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.CAPACITY.COMPARE_CAPACITY.mastery: The child pours water from one container into another to say which holds more, less or the same, does not judge by height alone, and re-uses containers to keep items.
MATH.G1.MEASUR.CAPACITY.COMPARE_CAPACITY.hands_on: Collecting, filling and re-using containers is done in class and at home.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_ARBITRAR.mastery: The child fills a basin or jug with a small container (a cup, a tin), counts the full cups, and compares two containers by their cup counts.
MATH.G1.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_ARBITRAR.hands_on: Filling basins with small containers is done in class.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.TIME.DAYS_OF_WEEK.mastery: The child says and writes the seven days of the week in order starting from any day, says which day comes before and after a given day, and counts on days (in 3 days from Monday it is Thursday), using today, yesterday and tomorrow.

forms: what do we do on Monday
MATH.G1.MEASUR.TIME.DAYS_ACTIVITIES.mastery: The child names what happens on particular days (raising the flag on Monday and Friday, no school on Saturday and Sunday, church or mosque day, market day) and says the day for an activity.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.TIME.MONTHS_OF_YEAR.mastery: The child says the twelve months in order (with a song), names the month of their birthday, and says which month comes before and after a given month.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.MONEY.IDENTIFY_COINS.mastery: The child names the Kenyan coins (sh. 1, sh. 5, sh. 10, sh. 20) by the number on them, sorts coins by value, and says which of two coins is worth more.

forms: is the note worth more than a sh. 20 coin
MATH.G1.MEASUR.MONEY.IDENTIFY_50_NOTE.mastery: The child recognises the sh. 50 note, says its value, and tells it from the coins.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.MONEY.COUNT_COINS.mastery: The child counts coins of one kind and then a mix (two sh. 10 coins and one sh. 5 coin is sh. 25) by counting on the value of each coin, and says how many coins there are and how much they are worth as two different things.

MATH.G1.MEASUR.MONEY.BUY_TWO_ITEMS.mastery: The child finds the cost of up to 2 items in a model shop (total up to sh. 50) and picks coins or the note that pay exactly, with no change.
MATH.G1.MEASUR.MONEY.BUY_TWO_ITEMS.hands_on: Role play in the classroom model shop is done in class.

forms: find a straight line in the picture
MATH.G1.GEOMET.LINES.IDENTIFY_LINES.mastery: The child says whether a line or an edge is straight or curved (a queue of children, the edge of a door, a semicircle, the rim of a plate) and finds straight and curved lines in real objects.

MATH.G1.GEOMET.LINES.DRAW_LINES.mastery: The child draws straight lines by joining two points with a stick or ruler, and curved lines freehand, on the ground and in books.
MATH.G1.GEOMET.LINES.DRAW_LINES.hands_on: Drawing lines on the ground and in books is done in class, with the teacher checking.

MATH.G1.GEOMET.SHAPES.IDENTIFY_SHAPES.mastery: The child names rectangles, triangles and circles in objects and pictures (a door, a roof, a clock), in any position, by their sides and corners (a triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners; a circle has none).

MATH.G1.GEOMET.SHAPES.SHAPE_PATTERNS_1.mastery: The child copies, continues and makes a repeating pattern of shapes (circle, triangle, circle, triangle) and says which shape comes next.
MATH.G1.GEOMET.SHAPES.SHAPE_PATTERNS_1.hands_on: Making and colouring shape patterns is done in class.
